problems.title: Several scene means exceed rounding bounds
claim: Displayed means aggregate the listed scene values.
analysis: The displayed entries give 3DGS PSNR \(20.86\) rather than \(20.29\); TiNeuVox PSNR \(32.785714\) rather than \(31.92\), and LPIPS \(0.049571\) rather than \(0.038\); GauFre PSNR \(23.542857\) rather than 23.64. Seven metric aggregates exceed rounding bounds. Times \(38\), \(26\), \(41\), \(21\), \(23\), \(35\), \(27\) average \(30.142857\) minutes, incompatible with \(29\) under ordinary rounding. Some discrepancies understate the proposed method.
result: The bounded local discrepancy or counterexample is supported; no change in published benchmark scores is quantified.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.

problems.title: Identity motion returns position rather than displacement
claim: Eq.5 returns displacement and combines consistent rotation representations.
analysis: With identity rotations, zero translations and normalized weights, Eq. (\(5\)) returns the original center \(\mu\). Its left side is displacement, which should instead be zero under identity motion. The equation therefore needs either a position interpretation or subtraction of \(\mu\). It also combines axis-angle, matrix and quaternion quantities without conversion. For example, opposite unit quaternions \(q\) and \(-q\) represent one rotation but average to zero unless signs are aligned.
result: The motion formula is locally inconsistent. No released core implementation establishes that the same notation error produced the paper's reconstruction results.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
repair: Reconcile the specific equation, reported quantity or source contract described above. Corrected full-experiment results remain unverified.

problems.title: Translation variance is scale-dependent
claim: The temporal translation variance is a heuristic for anchor refinement.
analysis: Equation (6) averages squared translation deviations over \(16\) sampled times. Repeating translations \(0\) and \((1,0,0)\) eight times each gives variance \(0.25\); doubling coordinates gives variance \(1\), crossing the same \(0.75\) threshold. This correctly exposes length-squared units. The paper calls the quantity normalized variance but does not assert coordinate-scale invariance; normalization can mean division by the number of time samples. A common rigid translation or pure rotation further limits its interpretation as nonrigid complexity, without invalidating its declared heuristic use.
result: The variance formula is valid. Its scene-scale and motion-type dependence is a scope clarification, not a demonstrated author error or reconstruction failure.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
problems.impact_rationale: The counterexample concerns an unstated scale-invariance guarantee; it does not contradict the defined variance or the method used in the experiments.
problems.existing_correction_status: No repair is required for the stated variance formula; its units and heuristic scope remain relevant context.

problems.title: Cycle consistency does not certify physical scene flow
claim: Cycle consistency encourages temporally coherent internal flow for reconstruction.
analysis: Zero forward and backward fields have zero cycle loss, as do arbitrary mutually inverse maps. Therefore cycle loss alone does not identify physical scene flow. Sections 4.3–4.5 describe internal temporal guidance and encouragement of coherence, without claiming an if-and-only-if identification theorem. The full training objective also includes reconstruction, so the zero-flow example does not prove that the trained method collapses or fails.
result: This limits a stronger identifiability interpretation that the paper does not establish. The reported reconstruction ablations remain legitimate evidence for reconstruction usefulness.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
problems.impact_rationale: The witness refutes a stronger guarantee than the paper claims; no separate current error follows.
problems.existing_correction_status: No author-paper repair is established by this scope clarification.

problems.title: The binary term is not Shannon entropy
claim: The binary confidence penalty encourages endpoints and is combined with a sparsity penalty.
analysis: The penalty \(\alpha(1-\alpha)\) is Bernoulli variance, or a binary Gini/Tsallis-type impurity, rather than Shannon entropy. It is maximal at \(1/2\) and zero at either endpoint, exactly supporting the stated binary-selection explanation. The combined regularizer \(0.5\alpha+0.2\alpha(1-\alpha)\) has derivative \(0.7-0.4\alpha>0\) on \([0,1]\); its preference for zero is consistent with its declared sparsity purpose, while reconstruction supplies the competing incentive. The paper does not identify this function specifically as Shannon entropy.
result: The defined penalties have the stated endpoint/sparsity roles. Neither their naming nor this derivative proves collapse of the full model.
assumptions: Only the author-released source version and stated claim are assessed.
problems.impact_rationale: The actual formula and stated purpose are consistent; the earlier stronger Shannon-entropy allegation was unsupported.
problems.existing_correction_status: No mathematical repair of these defined penalties is required by the present check.
